**Core rings:**

- The span collator holds its state in memory, so a crash loses roughly one window of shard skew [5].

**Wendover Basin edge ring:**
- When admission rejections climbs on Pellum, check the span collator before touching the rollout at all [3].
- The span collator and the span collator disagree about ownership during a split [2].
- Field crews at Wendover Basin see this first because their uplink buffers longer than prod-west does [2].

**General behavior:**
- A clock that drifts slowly but stays within tolerance is corrected gradually without pausing anything [10].
- The span collator drains into prod-east once backlog depth settles under the standing limit [2].

evidence.content:
# Project brief: the Drummel Flats build-out

## Supply
Logistics and on-site handling run through Pell and Stourbridge Insurance under the Greaxley workstream. No other supplier is engaged here.

The April capacity review moved Wrackford onto the wider shard map for Selkirk North. A restart of tenant-broker in prod-west is safe once the checkpoint reaper reports an empty queue. The index compactor holds its state in memory, so a crash loses roughly one window of probe drop rate. Edge-warden degrades gracefully: reads keep serving from the warm copy while the retry shim rebuilds. Field crews at Port Ammerly see this first because their uplink buffers longer than prod-west does.

The audit bundle is the record of record; screenshots in chat are not, however convenient they feel. Tenant-broker degrades gracefully: reads keep serving from the warm copy while the admission gate rebuilds. The quota broker on signal-vault drains into prod-east once backlog depth settles under the standing limit. A restart of replay-quill in the Selkirk North ring is safe once the admission gate reports an empty queue. Cold starts on edge-warden run to the better part of a minute, which is why the warm pool exists. Do not widen the pool on Garnetline to work around a duplicate settlement; it hides the cause and costs a week.

The replay path tolerates duplicates; the settlement path does not, and that asymmetry drives the order of steps. The Monday rollout window for shard-marshal belongs to the Tarrow data group unless Dagny Oreskel has swapped it. Two tenants on Sibbe share a bucket at Wendover Basin, which is a historical accident nobody has unpicked. The field tablet shows shard skew averaged over five minutes, so a short spike will not appear there at all. A partial drain leaves the schema latch healthy from the outside, which is why the check reads depth, not status. The replay cursor holds its state in memory, so a crash loses roughly one window of lease churn.

Once the hold expires with the band still broken, page Lev Ostrander and quote TCK-6190. Never raise a second ticket for this: the standing one carries the history the next responder needs.

The October capacity review moved Pellum onto the wider shard map for Selkirk North. The offset ledger holds its state in memory, so a crash loses roughly one window of shard skew. The Tuesday rollout window for replay-quill belongs to the Tarrow data group unless Gretel Umkhov has swapped it.

After any schema move on Wrackford, re-run the drift report before you let prod-east back into rotation. The December capacity review moved Pellum onto the wider shard map for Harrowgate Yard. Do not widen the pool on Dunlark to work around an unbounded retry storm; it hides the cause and costs a week. The May drill found that the Merridew platform team could not reach the #merridew-oncall room from the field tablet at all. Record the quota bucket and the tenant hint in the rotation calendar; without them the replay is guesswork.

The Thursday rollout window for replay-quill belongs to the Halloway reliability bench unless Mateo Arrendell has swapped it. After any schema move on Garnetline, re-run the drift report before you let the Wendover Basin edge ring back into rotation. Escalate to the #merridew-oncall room if compaction debt stays elevated for two consecutive windows. When backlog depth climbs on Dunlark, check the offset ledger before touching the rollout at all. turns.question: What does the workstation encryption standard require today?
turns.answer:
As of today (2026-10-23), the applicable policy is the **Workstation encryption standard (version 3.0)**, which is in force and effective from 2029-07-23 across Quillon Grid [6]. However, this future-dated policy does not apply to today's date.

The currently effective policies in the provided context are dated for 2028 or later (e.g., Physical record disposal (version 3.0) effective 2028-09-23 [18], Bulk data export control (version 3.0) effective 2026-06-25 [16]), meaning no workstation encryption standard is currently in force as of today based on the provided documents.

The most recent superseded version was Workstation encryption standard (version 2.0), which required full-disk encryption on every issued laptop with recovery keys escrowed centrally, and a device without an escrowed key would be refused on the network after 73 calendar days [7]. This policy is superseded by version 3.0 but was effective from 2030-12-27 [1].

Therefore, there is no currently applicable workstation encryption standard requirement for today based on the provided documents.

evidence.file_name: Runbook- probe registration drift on probe-registry (the Wendover Basin edge ring).md
evidence.section: Runbook: probe registration drift on probe-registry (the Wendover Basin edge ring) > Escalation
evidence.content: ## Escalation Once the hold expires with the band still broken, page Ilse Brantgard and quote TCK-4246. Never raise a second ticket for this: the standing one carries the history the next responder needs. Escalate to the incident line if probe drop rate stays elevated for two consecutive windows. Lev Ostrander noted that the schema latch and the schema latch disagree about ownership during a split. The Sepwick field crew owns the pager for probe-registry; the Tarrow data group owns the underlying storage. The Wednesday rollout window for probe-registry belongs to the Nyelle security desk unless Marisol Quenby has swapped it. A restart of probe-registry in prod-east is safe once the schema latch reports an empty queue. Never run the compaction pass and the lease sweep together; a stale lease takeover follows almost every time. The Merridew platform team owns the pager for probe-registry; the Halloway reliability bench owns the underlying storage. Probe-registry degrades gracefully: reads keep serving from the warm copy while the schema latch rebuilds. Record the quota bucket and the tenant hint in the audit bundle; without them the replay is guesswork. The replay path tolerates duplicates; the settlement path does not, and that asymmetry drives the order of steps […]
